title: UPDATE: Inquest will review police killing of Phonesay Chanthachack
subtitle: An inquest has been called into the 2012 death of a Hamilton man shot by police while at the wheel of a stolen van.
article: An inquest has been called into the 2012 death of a Hamilton man shot by police while at the wheel of a stolen van.
Dr. Roger Skinner, interim Deputy Chief Coroner for Investigations, announced the inquiry Tuesday.
Phonesay Chanthachack, 27, died on Feb. 13 at Hamilton General Hospital. An inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act.

Chanthachack died just four hours after a warrant was issued for his arrest. The man, nicknamed Pun, had skipped out on a court appearance that morning where he was facing 18 charges including break and enter, identity theft and credit card theft.
Police were in the area of Quigley and Albright roads early that afternoon when they encountered Chanthachack in a beige van.
According to the Special Investigations Unit, an arms-length agency that probes death or serious injury involving police, Chanthachack was blocked in an Albright Road parking lot by police cruisers.
He drove at Hamilton Constable Ryan Tocher, who fatally shot him through the passenger side window.
Tocher, who had gotten out of his vehicle to arrest Chanthachack and was struck by the van, was cleared of any wrongdoing by the SIU last June.
The inquest will examine the events surrounding Chanthachack's death. The jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar ones.
The inquest is expected to last 10 days and to hear from approximately 15 witnesses.
It is scheduled to begin at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, June 3, at the John Sopinka Courthouse, 45 Main St. E.
Dr. Jack Stanborough will preside as inquest coroner and Graeme Leach will be counsel to the coroner.
